title: Signed coordinate paths give the cubical coordinate homotopies
statement:
Let $r\geq0$ be an integer, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, and $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ its ordered standard basis. For $0\leq a\leq r$ let $C_a$ be the free abelian group [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on $[v,I]$ with $v\in D$, $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and $|I|=a$, and set $C_a=0$ in all other integer degrees. Put $q_i(I)=\#\{j\in I:j<i\}$ and define homomorphisms by
$$\partial_a[v,I]=\sum_{i\in I}(-1)^{q_i(I)}([v+u_i,I\setminus\{i\}]-[v,I\setminus\{i\}])\quad(a\geq1),\qquad \partial_a=0\quad(a\leq0).$$
For $1\leq i\leq r$ set $\rho_i(v)=v-v_i u_i$ and define $p_{i,a}:C_a\to C_a$ by $p_{i,a}[v,I]=0$ when $i\in I$ and $p_{i,a}[v,I]=[\rho_i(v),I]$ otherwise, with zero maps outside the range. For a family $b:\mathbf Z\to A$ in any abelian group $A$ define the finite signed sum
$$\Sigma_n b=\begin{cases}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}b(k)&n>0,\\0&n=0,\\-\sum_{k=n}^{-1}b(k)&n<0.\end{cases}$$
For every integer $n$ these sums satisfy
$$\Sigma_n\bigl(b(k+1)-b(k)\bigr)=b(n)-b(0),\qquad\Sigma_{n+1}b-\Sigma_n b=b(n).$$
For $1\leq i\leq r$ define maps on basis elements in degree $a$ by
$$H_{i,a}[v,I]=\begin{cases}(-1)^{q_i(I)}\Sigma_{v_i}\bigl(k\mapsto[\rho_i(v)+ku_i,I\cup\{i\}]\bigr)&i\notin I,\\0&i\in I.\end{cases}$$
These formulas extend to homomorphisms $H_{i,a}:C_a\to C_{a+1}$, zero for $a=r$ and outside $0\leq a\leq r$. In every integer degree,
$$\partial_{a+1}H_{i,a}+H_{i,a-1}\partial_a=1-p_{i,a}.$$
More explicitly, for $i\notin I$ the left side at $[v,I]$ is $[v,I]-[\rho_i(v),I]$, while for $i\in I$ it is $[v,I]$. The formulas and identities hold for all signs of $v_i$, including $v_i=-1,0$, and in top degree. No translation equivariance of $H_{i,a}$ is asserted.

proof.text: First verify the signed-sum recurrence directly from the three cases defining $\Sigma$. If $n\geq1$, adjoining the last summand gives $\Sigma_{n+1}b-\Sigma_n b=b(n)$. For $n=0$ this is $b(0)-0=b(0)$. If $n\leq-2$, the difference is $-\sum_{k=n+1}^{-1}b(k)+\sum_{k=n}^{-1}b(k)=b(n)$; at $n=-1$ it is $0-(-b(-1))=b(-1)$. Thus the recurrence holds for every integer, without any division or ordering assumption on the abelian group.

proof.text: For $n>0$, cancelling successive terms in $\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(b(k+1)-b(k))$ leaves $b(n)-b(0)$. For $n<0$, the unsigned sum from $n$ to $-1$ is $b(0)-b(n)$, so its negative is again $b(n)-b(0)$; for $n=0$ both sides vanish. These are the first signed-sum identities in the statement. Finite distributivity also gives $\Sigma_n(b+c)=\Sigma_n b+\Sigma_n c$, $\Sigma_n(-b)=-\Sigma_n b$, and $f(\Sigma_n b)=\Sigma_n(f\circ b)$ for every homomorphism $f$, in all three cases of the definition.

proof.text: For $0\leq a<r$ and $i\notin I$, the displayed $H$ formula is a finite sum of basis vectors of $C_{a+1}$: $I\cup\{i\}$ has cardinality $a+1$. For $i\in I$ it is zero. By the unique finite expansion in a basis in [def-weil-pbc-free-module], explicitly send $\sum m_{v,I}[v,I]$ to $\sum m_{v,I}H_{i,a}[v,I]$; uniqueness makes this well-defined, and addition of coefficients proves additivity. This constructs the claimed homomorphism, without invoking an unstated universal-property theorem. In degree $r$ every basis subset contains $i$, so this formula is zero; outside the range use the unique zero map. The same extension argument justifies the basis formulas for $\partial$ and $p_i$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; the finite signed-coordinate calculation here is agent-written.

proof.text: Fix $i\notin I$, put $n=v_i$, $w=\rho_i(v)$, and $J=I\cup\{i\}$. In $\partial H_{i,a}[v,I]$, the face deleting $i$ has sign $(-1)^{q_i(I)+q_i(J)}=1$ since $q_i(J)=q_i(I)$. Its contribution is therefore $\Sigma_n(k\mapsto[w+(k+1)u_i,I]-[w+ku_i,I])=[v,I]-[w,I]$ by step 2. This remains valid for $n<0$ and $n=0$. It remains to cancel the faces deleting $j\in I$ against $H_{i,a-1}\partial_a$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; the finite signed-coordinate calculation here is agent-written.

proof.text: For each $j\in I$ (so $j\ne i$), the $j$-face in $\partial H[v,I]$ is $(-1)^A\Sigma_n(k\mapsto[w+ku_i+u_j,J\setminus\{j\}]-[w+ku_i,J\setminus\{j\}])$, where $A=q_i(I)+q_j(J)$. The $j$-face in $H\partial[v,I]$ is the very same signed sum multiplied by $(-1)^B$, where $B=q_j(I)+q_i(I\setminus\{j\})$: indeed $(v+u_j)_i=n$ and $\rho_i(v+u_j)=w+u_j$. Counting elements below an index gives $q_j(J)=q_j(I)+\mathbf1_{i<j}$ and $q_i(I\setminus\{j\})=q_i(I)-\mathbf1_{j<i}$. Hence $A-B=\mathbf1_{i<j}+\mathbf1_{j<i}=1$, so the two coefficients are opposite. Explicitly, if $i<j$ then $A=q_i(I)+q_j(I)+1$ and $B=q_i(I)+q_j(I)$; if $j<i$ then $A=q_i(I)+q_j(I)$ and $B=q_i(I)+q_j(I)-1$. They cancel for every $j$, using the finite-sum additivity of step 2 even when $n<0$. If $I$ is empty, there are no such faces and $\partial_0=0$. Along with step 4 this gives $[v,I]-[\rho_i(v),I]$ whenever $i\notin I$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; the finite signed-coordinate calculation here is agent-written.

proof.text: Now suppose $i\in I$ and put $K=I\setminus\{i\}$, $n=v_i$, $w=\rho_i(v)$. Here $H[v,I]=0$. Every face of $\partial[v,I]$ deleting $j\ne i$ still contains $i$, so its image under $H$ vanishes. For the remaining face, $q_i(K)=q_i(I)$, $\rho_i(v+u_i)=w$ and $(v+u_i)_i=n+1$. Thus its two signs multiply to $1$, and $H\partial[v,I]=\Sigma_{n+1}(k\mapsto[w+ku_i,I])-\Sigma_n(k\mapsto[w+ku_i,I])=[v,I]$ by step 1. This calculation applies also in top degree $a=r$, where $H_{i,r}=0$, and at $n=-1$ or $0$. At $n=-1$ the surviving expression is $0-(-[w-u_i,I])=[v,I]$; at $n=0$ it is $[w,I]-0=[v,I]$. Thus a vanishing path at the origin does not make the homotopy identity vanish on a cube containing $i$.

source.place: Tag 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), preceding alternating differential, comparison only; the finite signed-coordinate calculation here is agent-written.

proof.text: Steps 4--6 give $\partial_{a+1}H_{i,a}+H_{i,a-1}\partial_a=1-p_{i,a}$ on every basis vector in each degree $0\leq a\leq r$. Equality on arbitrary elements follows by applying both homomorphisms to the unique finite expansion in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For $a<0$ or $a>r$ the source group $C_a$ is zero, so both sides are the unique map out of zero; this includes the adjacent degrees $-1,r+1$. At $a=0$ the term through $C_{-1}$ is zero, as already used in step 5. If $r=0$, there is no index $1\leq i\leq r$, and the homotopy assertions are vacuous; the signed-sum assertions remain those of steps 1--2. All sums used were finite. No claim of translation equivariance was used or deduced.
